summary: Hopkins Mountain tower, Greenbrier County, WV: CCC-built 1935, removed 1979. The observer's cabin survives, restored 2016 and rentable since 2017.

facts.design: Fire tower with an observer's cabin on the same site; sources give the cabin as 14 by 13 ft or 14 by 20 ft
facts.status_note: The tower was removed in 1979; the observer's cabin still stands and was made available for rentals in 2017.
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Monongahela National Forest

access.note: The cabin is a Forest Service recreation site. A locked gate blocked the last few hundred yards of the road in 2020 (Bitter Southerner account); current gate status not verified.

events.note: Built with Civilian Conservation Corps labor; the Forest Service and Bitter Southerner credit the CCC with the cabin, tower site and road
Register: removed in 1979. No source describes remains at the site.
Observer's cabin made available for rentals
Registered January 26, 2017, as FFLOS US 1669, WV 60

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register's 3,318 ft (1,011 m) is for the tower site; the Forest Service's 3,162 ft is for the cabin. The two sets of coordinates also differ, so these appear to be different points, not one disputed figure.

notes_for_editor: Unresolved: cabin size (14 x 13 ft per Bitter Southerner, 14 x 20 ft per USFS); distance from White Sulphur Springs (USFS gives 17 mi in its summary and 15 mi in its directions); road length (USFS about 4 mi, Bitter Southerner about 5 mi). The 2017 Charleston Gazette-Mail article (wvgazettemail.com, 'Renovated fire tower cabin converted into getaway') returned HTTP 429 twice; retry it for the rental details and the 1935 photo caption. Search snippets only, not cited: recreation.gov listing, USFS Facebook rental reminder, WCHS 'Traveling WV' piece (says USFS restored the cabin and it is now available to rent). Current gate status, rental status and any tower remains are unverified. No source gives who staffed the tower or any fires it watched. Record status 'gone' is right for the tower but the cabin stands, so the status note carries that. No corrections proposed. The 2020 caretaker account is one writer's first-person feature, so treat its access details as dated.
